title: AI Tool Selection — Q2 2026 Engineering Stack
description: Eight candidate AI tools under review for adoption by the engineering team. Decide which to approve, reject, defer to next quarter, or skip. Notes welcome on conditions or alternatives.
query_description: All AI tools in the evaluation queue with completed trial reports

records.title: Claude Code
records.description: CLI-based AI coding assistant from Anthropic. Strong at multi-file edits, agentic tasks, and complex refactoring across large codebases.
records.context: Trialed by 6 engineers over 4 weeks. Most reported significant time savings on routine refactoring and test writing.
evidence_for: Average 32% reduction in time-to-merge for refactor PRs
Handles multi-file context better than line-by-line tools
Integrates with existing terminal workflows
Strong at writing tests against existing code
evidence_against: Token costs ~$80/engineer/month at current usage
Occasional incorrect edits requiring careful review
Learning curve for prompting effectively

records.title: GitHub Copilot Workspace
records.description: GitHub's task-based AI workspace for translating issues into pull requests with multi-step planning and editing.
records.context: Two engineers tested for 3 weeks. Limited adoption due to overlap with existing tooling.
evidence_for: Tight GitHub integration with native issue linking
Reasonable PR-quality output for small tasks
Already covered by org-wide GitHub Enterprise license
evidence_against: Weaker than Claude Code on complex multi-file changes
Limited terminal/CLI access during planning phase
Most engineers preferred their current setup

records.title: Cursor
records.description: AI-first code editor based on VS Code with deep model integration, including Cmd-K, agent mode, and codebase indexing.
records.context: Mixed reception. Strong individual results but causes IDE fragmentation across the team.
evidence_for: Excellent inline editing with Cmd-K
Strong codebase indexing for cross-file context
Many engineers report 'love it' satisfaction
evidence_against: Forks VS Code — diverges from team standard setup
$20/engineer/month on top of existing IDE costs
Shared keybindings/extensions config gets harder to maintain

records.title: Linear AI
records.description: Linear's built-in AI for triage, duplicate detection, sprint planning suggestions, and issue summarization.
records.context: Already enabled for free on existing Linear subscription. Used informally for 2 months.
evidence_for: Zero additional cost
Saves PM team ~3 hours/week on triage
Issue summaries are accurate and well-formatted
evidence_against: Limited to Linear's data — no cross-tool context
Some duplicate-detection false positives

records.title: Granola
records.description: Background meeting note-taker with transcription, automatic summary generation, and integration with note systems.
records.context: Privacy review required before approval. Data residency in US-East.
evidence_for: Transcription quality is excellent for our accent diversity
Saves meeting organizers ~2 hours/week
Markdown export integrates with our docs setup
evidence_against: Privacy review still pending — meetings may include customer data
$18/user/month adds up across the team
Some users find background recording invasive

records.title: Perplexity Pro
records.description: AI-powered research assistant with citations, web search integration, and follow-up question chaining.
records.context: Several engineers and PMs use the free tier informally. Pro upgrade under consideration.
evidence_for: Strong citation accuracy compared to other tools
Useful for technology surveys and competitive research
$20/user/month for unlimited Pro queries
evidence_against: Free tier already covers most use cases
Overlap with Claude's web search capabilities
Hard to justify org-wide rollout vs. ad-hoc personal subscriptions

records.title: v0 by Vercel
records.description: AI UI generation tool that produces React components and Tailwind layouts from natural language prompts.
records.context: Design team trialed for two prototype projects. Output quality variable.
evidence_for: Fast UI prototyping — from idea to clickable mockup in minutes
Output uses our existing Tailwind setup
Helps designers communicate intent to engineers
evidence_against: Generated code rarely production-ready without rework
Better for exploration than final deliverables
Figma still preferred for full design specs

records.title: Notion AI
records.description: AI features built into Notion workspace: writing assistance, summarization, Q&A across docs, and database autofill.
records.context: Notion is already the team's docs platform. AI add-on is $10/user/month.
evidence_for: Zero setup — works on existing docs
Q&A feature surfaces buried info effectively
Improves consistency of meeting notes and one-pagers
evidence_against: Adds $10/user/month to existing Notion bill
Q&A quality depends on docs being kept current
Overlap with Granola for meeting summaries
